A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

stubble retention and minimum tillage, particularly zero tillage, can be used to improve soil water storage in a wide range of soils in semi arid environments, provided that the rainfall regime is sufficient to allow for the accumulation of soil water.
zero tillage with stubble retention is a viable alternative to conventional tillage in the semi arid environment.
stubble retention, particularly with zero tillage, is an effective strategy for improving water storage and hence wheat yield in semi arid areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the retention of stubble in zero tillage is an important management strategy for the conservation of soil moisture and the improvement of water use efficiency in the dryland farming systems of the semi arid zone of southern Australia.
